issues.description: Field 'lectureName' has a type mismatch across artifacts. The problem statement UML declares lectureName: String (problem_statement.md line 64). The template expects students to add a String attribute (TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 4 TODO). The solution implements a LectureName value object and declares the field as 'private LectureName lectureName;' (SOLUTION_REPOSITORY src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 6) and uses LectureName as the constructor parameter (SOLUTION_REPOSITORY src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13). However, the solution's getter and setter signatures are declared using String (getLectureName() declared to return String at SOLUTION_REPOSITORY src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 22; setLectureName(String) declared at line 26) while the backing field is LectureName, and the solution also provides a separate LectureName class (SOLUTION_REPOSITORY src/de/tum/cit/ase/LectureName.java line 3). This inconsistency causes compilation errors and confuses students about the expected type for lectureName and the correct constructor/getter/setter signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the lectureName type consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferred for minimal change): change the solution to use a String field for lectureName and update the constructor parameter and getter/setter to String so the code matches the UML and template. Option B (if the LectureName value object is intentional): update the problem statement UML and the template to declare lectureName: LectureName and change all constructor, getter and setter signatures and documentation to use LectureName consistently. In either case ensure the field type and all method signatures match so the code compiles (e.g., getLectureName() should return the same type as the lectureName field, and setLectureName(...) should accept that same type).
